findings.title: Backup codes are overwritten and returned before 2FA is enabled
findings.body: The setup endpoint generates new backup codes, persists them and returns them in plaintext, all before the TOTP code is verified. If a user cancels setup, the stored codes remain on the account. Because twoFactorEnabled is false, they are unused for now, but they stay valid secrets. If 2FA is later enabled by another path, they apply. Codes should be generated at enable time, or cleared when setup is cancelled.

findings.title: Disable endpoint does not guard against non-string backupCode or malformed data
findings.body: `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll(...)` throws a 500 if backupCode is not a string, for example a number or an object sent in the JSON body. `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` is also unguarded. Validate that the input is a string first. In addition, consumed codes are nulled in the login flow, and `indexOf` on user input could match a null or empty entry if the input is odd.

findings.title: Backup code check has no format validation and a non-atomic consume
findings.body: `credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")` is compared with plain `indexOf`. This is not constant-time, though that is minor. More importantly, consuming the code is a read-modify-write, so two concurrent requests with the same code can both succeed. Also, the existing condition `user.password && !credentials.totpCode` skips the password check whenever totpCode is empty. Passing a backupCode with no totpCode therefore works, but a TOTP code with a wrong password still skips the password check. This pre-existing behavior is now extended by the backup path.

findings.title: Modal state and the blob URL are not cleaned up after the backup codes are shown
findings.body: resetState does not clear backupCodes, the blob URL, the secret or dataUri. The object URL is never revoked on close or unmount, so a leak remains. The plaintext codes also stay in component state after the dialog closes. Also, onOpenChange (clicking the overlay or pressing Esc) closes the dialog on the backup codes step without calling resetState, so the next open may resume at the backup codes step.

findings.title: Component is misnamed TwoFactor
findings.body: The default export in BackupCode.tsx is named `TwoFactor`, which duplicates the name of the other component and is confusing in stack traces and devtools.

findings.title: Lost access toggle button lacks type="button"
findings.body: The Button defaults to type submit inside the Form, so clicking 'Lost access' or 'Go back' may submit the form. The submit would carry validation of the required fields, such as the backup code, and could trigger an unwanted disable request. Set type="button". The same applies to the Cancel button.
